value.hook: When installing over a running daemon binary or deriving future child execs from current_exe
value.title: Atomic executable replacement preserves code but not current_exe path lifetime

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Atomic replacement proves two different lifetimes: the old process can keep executing its open inode, but its later current_exe() result may no longer name an executable file. On Linux an unlinked/replaced process image is reported by /proc/self/exe with " (deleted)" appended. A daemon that obtains current_exe afresh to launch child observers must account for that when installers rename over its executable.

#229 63a2ba523c2a104ff418f3f1d7baaa37a47cda11 was blocked in round 1 on P229-F001: install-pij-rs.sh renames over the copy on every install; http/mod.rs:1547 obtains current_exe on every spawn; harnesses/spawn.rs:290 forwards it unchanged. An unchanged/cached rs-install now also retires the running copy's inode. The hard-link fixture only proves that old bytes survive, not that the existing process can later exec a child. This is a source/ABI finding, not a passed-repair receipt or a reviewer-run live test.

Use the canonical verdict for details and exact-head CI evidence. Independent Linux ABI reference: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_exe.5.html. The missing proof surface is a live installed-process/reinstall/later-exec fixture, not another check of file contents.

Operational ruling received 2026-11-11 at 10:25: no local heavy build/test across any project without a granted machine-build baton, keeper pij-outstanding-silkworm; nice 19 remains. This review used source and CI only, without requesting a baton or running a local build/test.
